ENCODING

Base64URL decoder & encoder

Decode URL-safe Base64 to UTF-8 text or hex bytes. Encode text without padding, compare standard Base64 and download the original bytes locally.

URL-safe · RFC 4648

Paste one URL-safe value using A–Z, a–z, 0–9, - and _. Valid padded or unpadded input is accepted; whitespace is ignored. Up to 2 million encoded characters.

A LITTLE CONTEXT

How to decode Base64URL

Base64URL is the URL- and filename-safe alphabet defined in RFC 4648 section 5. It replaces the standard Base64 characters + and / with the ASCII hyphen - and underscore _. Paste one encoded value above and choose UTF-8 text or Hex bytes before decoding.

Base64URL: + → -   / → _   trailing = may be omitted

References: RFC 4648 §5: URL-safe alphabet · RFC 7519: JWT

Good to know

Is Base64URL the same as Base64?

Both represent the same bytes with 64 printable symbols. Their last two alphabet characters differ. Base64URL is a separate alphabet, not URL percent-encoding; this tool does not automatically decode % escapes.

Why does a valid value produce no text?

An encoded value can contain binary bytes that are not valid UTF-8. The tool then leaves the text result empty and explains the issue. Choose Hex bytes or download the original bytes. The standard Base64 comparison still represents the same bytes.

Can I decode a JWT?

Paste only one encoded segment from a token, such as a header or payload. A complete dot-separated token is not one Base64URL value. Decoding a segment does not verify a signature, validate claims or establish authenticity.

Are inputs uploaded or saved?

Conversion runs in your browser. The application does not upload inputs, store input history or put values in the URL. Clipboard and downloads are used only when you press their buttons. Normal website requests still go to the hosting provider.

PRACTICAL REFERENCE

Base64URL padding and validation

Missing padding can be reconstructed from a valid length. Padding alone cannot repair invalid characters, truncated data or non-zero trailing bits.

Length of the value after removing whitespace and trailing =
Length modulo 4Required padding for a padded representation
0No padding
2==
3=
1Invalid encoded length

Padded and unpadded input

Zg and Zg== both decode to f. Zg= is rejected because its explicit padding is incomplete. Encoding above omits padding by default; enable Add = padding if the receiving system requires it.

Strict alphabet checks

Use the ASCII hyphen -, not a typographic minus sign. Standard Base64 + and /, percent escapes and data URI prefixes are rejected here. Use the standard Base64 tool or image viewer for those input types.

Validate the final bits

Zg is the canonical encoding of f. Zh is rejected for non-zero unused trailing bits, even though a permissive decoder might return the same byte.

Text and byte limits

Decode up to 2 million encoded characters, including any whitespace. Encoding accepts up to 1 MB (1,000,000 bytes) of UTF-8 text. Bytes and text downloads are generated locally; downloading bytes does not identify or convert their file format.

PRACTICAL REFERENCE

Decode a known Base64URL value in JavaScript or Python

Both snippets decode the fixed, valid emoji example. They illustrate alphabet normalization, padding and UTF-8 decoding; the tool above also checks alphabet, length and unused trailing bits.

JavaScript: Base64URL to UTF-8

const value = '8J-YgA';
const standard = value.replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/');
const padded = standard + '='.repeat((4 - standard.length % 4) % 4);
const bytes = Uint8Array.from(atob(padded), c => c.charCodeAt(0));
new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true }).decode(bytes);
// 😀

Python: Base64URL to UTF-8

import base64

value = "8J-YgA"
padded = value + "=" * (-len(value) % 4)
base64.urlsafe_b64decode(padded).decode("utf-8")
# 😀

Base64URL is an encoding, so anyone with the value can decode it. It does not encrypt text or authenticate a token. Use Base64 encode / decode when you need the standard alphabet.
